artifacts.caption: FIG. 1 is a schematic presentation of a side cross-sectional view along Line A of FIG. 2 which depicts a zinc penetration test cell that is employed to determine the zinc penetration factors of the coated microporous membranes described herein. FIG. 2 is a schematic presentation of a top view of the same test cell of FIG. 1. The design of the zinc penetration test cell is shown in FIGS. 1 and 2. FIG. 1 depicts a side cross-sectional view along line A of FIG. 2. FIG. 2 depicts a top view looking down into the cell with its cover removed. With reference to the drawings four BB-461 silver-zinc ABS monoblock cell cases (12) are used to house the cell componentry. The inner cell dimensions are 0.730"±0.005" wide, 21/4" long and 3-3/16" high. The cell components include (a) 0.005" thick pure sheet zinc cathode (1), 21/2" high×13/4" wide clad as a "U" around a 0.005" sheet nickel current collector (2), 4" high (including a 11/2" high×1/4" wide tab (2')) and 13/4" wide, (b) four layers (depicted as one) of 0.005" thick corroding sheet zinc anode (3) folded in a "U", 21/2" high×11/2" wide and a sheet nickel current collector (4) 4" high (including 11/2"×1/4" tab (4')) and 11/2" wide, (c) a partially charged Ni(OH) 2 reference electrode (5), 0.028" thick, 11/4" high and 11/4" wide, juxtaposed against the sheet zince cathode (1), (d) 0.005" thick polyamide felt Pellon (6) cladding the sheet zinc cathode (1), (e) a "U" wrapped separator system (shown as the test separator system 7/8/7) enveloping said Ni(OH) 2 reference electrode (5) with the empty half of separator "U" being folded to the rear of the reference electrode and facing the corroding sheet zinc anode (3), (f) two lucite supporting blocks (9) and (9'), each 0.25" thick, 21/4" wide and 21/2" high, located between the corroding sheet zinc anode (3) and reference electrode (5) containing 7/8" diameter electrolyte channels, centrally located, and (g) lucite shims (10), located at the rear of the corroding anode. It is separator (8) which is varied as described herein.
